githubRelease.summary: Animonkey 1.3.0 fixes immediate profile image updates and refreshes the embedded Anivexa runtime and provider inventory.

sections.title: Profile image refresh
details: Uploading or removing a profile image now goes through the shared account state, so the updated image is reflected across views immediately without restarting the application.

sections.title: Embedded Anivexa runtime
details: The pinned runtime is updated from `fb337ea` to `c9e0b72`.
AniHQ and Pahenime replace the retired MKissa and Senshi provider entries. The update also fixes AniPM's domain and restores AnimeGG and AniKoto catalog matching.

sections.title: Provider integrations
details: The desktop provider inventory, monitor samples, and provider-failure allowlist now reflect the current runtime while retaining support for historical provider slugs in persisted notifications.

githubRelease.summary: Animonkey 1.2.0 adds clear feedback to meaningful user actions, refines header search suggestions, and reorganizes local notifications into four independent categories.

sections.title: Header search
details: The header search now has a softer focus indicator, restrained press feedback, animated suggestion entry, and clearer selected result rows.
The AniList query, five-result cap, debounce, adult-content preference, and keyboard combobox behavior remain unchanged. Reduced-motion preferences are respected.

sections.title: Action feedback
details: Accessible success, warning, and error toasts report meaningful outcomes across Watch Later, followed anime, ratings, sharing, account forms, backups, and saved preferences. Toasts stack at the bottom-right and pause dismissal while hovered or focused.
Action results are retained in the local notification history until users explicitly delete them. Failed preference writes restore the previous value and report the failure.

sections.title: Notification center
details: The notification center now opens as a floating, modeless panel and filters action feedback, system notices, anime and episode alerts, and update notifications independently.

Users can review unread items, mark notifications as read, open supported destinations, and delete action-history entries. Existing system and remote-feed behavior remains local-first and best effort.

sections.title: Motion and accessibility
details: Toast stacks and the notification panel use Motion transitions based on opacity and transforms. Reduced-motion preferences are respected, toasts remain keyboard accessible, and the panel supports Escape and outside-click dismissal.

githubRelease.summary: Animonkey 1.1.0 expands discovery, personalization, local notifications, privacy controls, playback guidance, and diagnostics.

sections.title: Discovery and catalog
details: Search now offers screenshot-based scene lookup from a header widget and a compact result preview. Pagination follows AniList's `hasNextPage` field and preserves the current scroll position when moving between result pages.
Discovery defaults to the global adult-content preference, with a safe-for-work default for new profiles. The per-search adult-content selector has been removed.

sections.title: Library, notifications, and privacy
details: Users can follow airing anime and receive local episode notifications. The notification center keeps read and dismissed state locally and can read a maintainer-controlled static Supabase Storage feed. Remote-feed failures are best effort and do not block local notifications or app startup.
Watch-history privacy controls let users review and clear locally stored history. Feedback intake supports suggestions and bug reports with explicit consent and server-side validation.

sections.title: Personalization and accessibility
details: Settings now include a title-language preference, configurable caption text size, global keyboard shortcuts, and configurable sidebar route ordering.
Navigation controls avoid accidental text selection, and discovery rails use the available width more effectively on wide screens.

sections.title: Playback and diagnostics
details: Anime finales surface continuation recommendations when catalog and provider episode evidence agree. Expected Anivexa request cancellations are handled without presenting them as provider failures.
The app includes an Anivexa diagnostics panel and an opt-in, authenticated report for selected provider lookup failures. Provider reports exclude anime IDs, provider URLs, and raw errors.

sections.title: Desktop reliability and release configuration
details: Production builds disable DevTools shortcuts while development builds retain them.

The Windows workflows pass the required public Supabase configuration explicitly into packaged builds and fail production packaging when required values are missing. No private service-role credential is bundled.

githubRelease.summary: Animonkey 1.0.3 refines desktop navigation and Settings, remembers player volume locally, caches Anivexa episode lists, and makes the update center easier to scan.

sections.title: Window navigation
details: Windows now uses the custom application title bar with in-app back and forward controls. The app also restores the last successfully visited internal route at startup, while explicit anime deep links take precedence ([custom window chrome](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/commit/ff6bc97), [route restoration](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/commit/45ffd94), [back and forward controls](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/commit/09359c9)).

sections.title: Settings experience
details: Settings is organized into sections for account and sync, Anivexa diagnostics, and local backup. The unavailable caption settings entry is hidden until the app supports configurable caption preferences ([Settings redesign](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/commit/fc60ecb), [caption settings adjustment](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/commit/d099019)).

sections.title: Playback preferences and episode cache
details: Player volume is stored through the existing IndexedDB-backed local preference store and restored across app sessions ([volume preference](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/commit/025ec1b)).

Anivexa episode lists are persisted client-side in the existing IndexedDB catalog cache. Expiry follows AniList airing data: after an expected episode time, missing episodes are retried hourly; once the episode appears, the cache follows the next weekly slot. Completed lists are retained for 30 days, and a failed refresh serves the previous list and retries after an hour ([episode-list cache](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/commit/6b06346)).

sections.title: Application update center
details: The update center opens on a compact version overview, identifies the installed version, and lets users select a release to read its concise app-facing notes. Existing update detection and install behavior remain in place ([update-center redesign](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/commit/80f94ae), [version overview](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/commit/b6f19f8)).

githubRelease.summary: Patch release focused on Anivexa runtime diagnostics, account-sync IPC validation, and a more verifiable Windows release process.

sections.title: Anivexa runtime diagnostics
details: Sanitized API error summaries continue through the diagnostics channel, while stderr receives a fixed redacted message instead of the original `console.error` arguments ([commit `13702a0`](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/commit/13702a0)).

sections.title: Account synchronization IPC
details: Watch-later upserts validate anime IDs, title shape, optional fields, episode counts, release dates, genres, and timestamps before reaching the account service.

Episode-progress upserts validate identifiers, non-negative episode numbers, finite time values, positive durations, and that current playback time does not exceed duration. Both validation paths were added in [commit `c5bf1de`](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/commit/c5bf1de).

sections.title: Windows packaging and release workflow
details: The application root MIT license is included as a packaged resource ([commit `502665a`](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/commit/502665a)).

The Windows package verifier checks the Setup installer, full Squirrel `.nupkg`, executable identity, required Anivexa runtime files and revision, package manifest, and `RELEASES` hash and size ([commit `591c1f4`](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/commit/591c1f4)).

Development CI runs Linux quality checks in one job and builds the Windows package only for a `dev`-to-`main` promotion pull request. The manual stable-release workflow builds the exact tag and creates a draft with the installer, full `.nupkg`, and `RELEASES` already attached. The release-pipeline redesign was integrated by [PR #1](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/pull/1) and promoted with [PR #2](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/pull/2). The split between concise app notes and detailed GitHub notes is tracked by [PR #3](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/pull/3) and its promotion in [PR #4](https://github.com/DaniHRE/animonkey-electron/pull/4).
